The game is riddled with bugs. Even when you dodge boss attacks, the game often fails to register them, despite the fact that you’re timing it perfectly. Sometimes the dodge counts and sometimes it doesn’t. Hits landed on enemies don’t always register either. You can stand right in front of an enemy and attack without dealing any damage. The story isn't particularly engaging. After the third chapter, I skipped all the cutscenes. As for the skill tree, I tested so many combinations that I feel it has a negligible impact on gameplay, which strikes me as odd. The same goes for potion crafting. They matter so little that I only used them a couple of times throughout the entire game just to see if they’d actually help. They do absolutely nothing. It makes no sense, why include a skill tree and potions that alter character stats by maybe 1%? It’s pointless. The only upside to this game is the graphics. Nothing else. I bought it on sale, and I still don't think it was worth the price. It certainly isn't worth the full amount. Unfortunately, I can't recommend Wukong. The game was hyped up by glowing reviews that must have been paid for because I can't see any other explanation.

Black Myth: Wukong is a great looking game. Sound design and music are als fantastic. Some bosses are very easy, others incredibely frustrating. While overcomming them gave some measure of satisfaction, the game always left me exhausted and just wanting it to end.
Thanks to a helpful guide and some tips both on steam and on youtube, I was able to achieve the game's secret ending, despite my lack of skill. I'm glad I finished the game, but I definitevely don't look forward to new game plus or the gauntlets unlocked with it.
The main reason I'm not recommending the game, however, it's the severe stuttering during cutscenes, making an already hard to follow story all the more confusing in my opinion. Couple that with the overabundance of invisible walls to give a "tech demo feel" to a game that should have seen much more polish by now. My character and the last boss spent much of the fight running against one such invisible wall, and an optional cart-like boss even managed to lock my character behind one.
The gameplay tends to drag on as well, mainly because there's next to no variety in playstyles. Sure, you have many armor sets with different bonuses, and many spells to spice up gameplay. But between mana costs, long cooldowns and clear early game unlockable superiority in most cases shift the burden on the player to try and force build variety. While the game hosts a huge cast of bosses with many unique moves, the gameplay loop almost always end the same: use a vessel, attack, use a spirit skill, attack, imobilize, spin to win, dodge around and build Qi if it's not full, rince and repeat. I'm glad it's over. just like this long-winded and boring review.

This game was surprisingly good! Far from your typical Souls-like, the depth of its combat styles and mechanics was incredible.

Although all of that was for naught, since I never used any spells or anything beyond the good old bonk. Not because I wanted to impose unnecessary restrictions on myself, but because the game allowed me to adapt its mechanics to my own playstyle. (I was damn happy when my friend showed me the spell that blocks all other spells in exchange for ridiculous amounts of damage.)

Beating the journey through sheer stubbornness and a stick was indeed a journey worthy of the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal!

(Getting the platinum trophy for this game was a headache, though. EVEN MORE GREAT SAGE-LIKE.)

My gaming career peaked with the flip phones. Since then it’s been a slow, undignified decline.

So I did not expect to love a game with a monkey and a stick. But here we are.

Wukong is hard. The first big boss flattened me so many times I started to feel bad for him. He had to keep doing the same victory pose for me. Still, I kept going back, because every death felt fair. I never thought “the game cheated.” I thought “ah, yes, I rolled directly into the giant swinging club.”

If you’re rusty, slow, or just plain bad, don’t let the difficulty scare you. Wukong lets you be terrible and still feel like the Monkey King. Just remember: you’re not losing, you’re monkeying around in the early stages of winning.

10/10. Will get bonked again.

From terrible gameplay and hitboxes over motion sickness (in a 3rd person game?????) all the way to a story even more confusing than any soulsborne game, this game is a mess. I refunded this once already because I hated the weirdly placed and highly restrictive invisible walls but decided to give it a 2nd shot. I can now say that I wholeheartedly regret spending that much money on a game I probably won't continue playing. 
The gameplay is sluggish. Animations are way to long with an input buffer that extends these periods even further making your life harder. Animation cancels are non existent. A dodge with 3 progressively longer animations looks cool but is impractical as hell. You're reliant on it tho, since there aren't real parries (there's a spell that kinda parries but there's a cooldown on it and it relies on mana which you can't refill until you rest. horrible design choice). There are 1000 different things to choose from in the skill tree which leaves you in a choice paralysis until you realize that most of these things are utter garbage you won't use anyway. There are stances which you can unlock by spending points which don't seem to offer any benefit at all. So why even bother???
Then there's the difficulty curve. The main areas are easy, every casual gamer should be able to breeze through there. I cleared everything unti I hit the final boss - a roadblock akin to Ornstein & Smough in DS1. Which truly made me think: where does BM:W want to position itself? That boss was annoying as hell because of the aforementioned things already but on top of it it had the biggest healthbar up until that point. And because he left very few openings, the battle was long. So if I was a casual gamer who managed to clear the game up until there, wtf am I supposed to do? You're >8h in atp, so you can't even refund. 
The next boss (which made me write this rant-y review) was the first one in the next area. It instantly one-hitted me with an attack. When I went in again I had to find out that the camera was playing against you because the boss was hardly in focus while most hits were a whiff due to the horrendous hitboxes. (I even ran into some enemies that weren't able to hit me despite standing literally inside me...) And since that boss was BIG, you had to run miles to get to the body parts you were able to hit. But until you reached that, he was on the run already. While I could use some spells, as I already mentioned, mana is laughably limited with no option to replenish mid fight. He also just walzes right through most attempts of "parrying/blocking", so that's some mana wasted. I didn't even try to fight him more than 5 times because I'm already pissed off beyond belief at this points.
Which is quite a shame because the visuals are GREAT, the game just does close to nothing with them. The world looks extremely cool and engaging but all you do is walk and fight, close to no interactions with anything whatsoever. The story could also be quite cool, especially the cutscenes seem great most times, but it feels very directionless. I don't even know the name of the protagonist, let alone what his main goal is. All I do is walk and fight. And those two are some of the weakest points of the game

I genuinely haven't had this much fun with a game in a while. Black Myth: Wukong was exactly what I needed, a great mix of soulslike and hack-and-slash combat, with a beautiful world, interesting bosses, and gameplay that kept me hooked.

The combat feels amazing. It's fast, satisfying, and there's enough variety in the abilities to experiment with different playstyles. But the bosses were definitely my favorite part. There are so many of them, and each one feels different. Some took me quite a few attempts to beat, but instead of getting frustrated, I usually just wanted to try again. And finally beating a boss after struggling for a while? That's exactly the feeling I love about soulslike games.

I also really enjoyed the world and its atmosphere. Chinese mythology looks absolutely gorgeous here, and some locations are so beautiful that I actually stopped just to look around. The side quests, hidden bosses, and secret areas were another pleasant surprise. I love games that don't constantly hold your hand and actually reward you for exploring.

Another thing I appreciated was how smooth the controls and camera felt. Even during difficult fights, I could focus on the boss instead of fighting against the game itself.

Overall, I had an amazing time playing it. For me, it's easily one of the best games that combines soulslike elements with hack-and-slash combat. It has pretty much everything I enjoy: challenging and spectacular bosses, rewarding exploration, a beautiful atmosphere, and a combat system that stays fun even after dozens of hours.
Definitely recommend it. I'd honestly love to play through it all over again.

One of the best souls-likes I've ever played. The combat system is just ... cool. You really only get 1 weapon, but each of the stances completely change the way you play. Different enemies will require you to use a different stance. Mastering the attack patterns, getting the perfect rock solid and seeing through the enemy's attacks is incredibly satisfying, and being offensive is rewarded.

The environments are stunning. I never felt like exploring a certain area was a waste. The secret areas are large and expansive and offer a ton of completely optional content. It never felt like the world had bloat at all. Enemy variety is great. There are barely any enemy types that are repeated. For the bosses, I'd say most bosses are not that hard, except for a couple where you're gonna die several times. But goddamn this game has a TON of bosses. And that is a good thing. My biggest complaint with elden ring for example is that unfortunately, that game has a lot of boss and enemy repetition, a.k.a. bloat, which is exactly why I prefer fromsoftware's linear games over that. This game however, does not have that problem, and is packed with content.

My biggest complaint honestly unlocking some achievements required you to do some absolute bs. You need to obtain items that are completely RNG-based so you'll have to farm certain locations OVER and OVER again and is no fun. But again, this is technically optional if you don't plan on 100%-ing the game.

But yea, absolutely do play this game. I don't usually beat a game 100%, but I felt this one deserved it.

As someone who played a lot of soulslike and souls adjacent games I really enjoyed this game.

Positives
-Great combat, game gives you a lot of tools and ways to play the game especially in the end game where you have access to alot of skills and transformations.
-Level Design was surprisingly good, for a linear game there is a lot of secret areas with good rewards. 
-Some of the best Boss Fights in gaming, eventhough theres so many bosses that sometimes the game feels like a boss rush game, the major boss battles at the end of each chapters are a spectacle specially some of the bosses in the end game.
-Soundtrack is not the most memorable one but there are bangers here and there, my personal favorite being the music from chapter 2 and the boss battle theme of the last hidden dragon boss fight.
-The Cinematics after every chapter is a good way to expand on the story that i would otherwise would have not understand at all, even now i dont fully understand the story XD

Negatives
-not a lot of things to say here except i expected more from the level design of the last chapter. also would have like access to the cloud for exploration on earlier chapters but it is what it is
